notes.japanese: つぶつぶと浮かんでゐる
notes.problem: Float in knobs is not English for clouds and stops the reader cold.
notes.sureness: Very sure as English; faithful reader need only confirmつぶつぶ is lumps not knobs.

notes.japanese: 畑と云ふ畑は、麻でも黍でも、皆、土いきれにぐつたりと頭をさげて
notes.problem: The that-is-a-field relative has to be read twice and sounds like machine literal.
notes.span: every field that is a field, hemp or millet, hangs its head limply in the rising heat from the earth
notes.suggestion: every field, hemp or millet, hangs its head limply in the heat rising from the earth
notes.sureness: Very sure as English; no Japanese doubt except whether the emphatic repetition needs keeping.

notes.japanese: 手ごろな素焼の瓶が一つ
notes.problem: Handy means convenient, not handy-sized, and reads like a dictionary swap.
notes.span: Then a handy unglazed earthen jar is set at this man's pillow,
notes.suggestion: Then a handy-sized unglazed earthen jar is set at this man's pillow,
notes.sureness: Very sure as English; faithful check need only confirm手ごろ means of a convenient size.

notes.japanese: 勿体らしくしやがんでゐる / 七面鳥のやうな恰好
notes.problem: Portentously promises the ominous while the simile is comic-pompous, so the voice slips.
notes.span: squats there portentously, in the attitude of a turkey.
notes.suggestion: squats there with ponderous self-importance, like a turkey.
notes.sureness: Fairly sure; if勿体らしい here carries menace rather than pomposity I am wrong.

notes.problem: Perfunctory describes an action, not a beard, and sounds learned in the wrong way.
notes.span: grows only a perfunctory beard like a rat's tail on the tip of his chin,
notes.suggestion: sports only a token beard, like a rat's tail, on the tip of his chin,
notes.sureness: Very sure as English; faithful reader need only confirm申訳だけ means token.

notes.japanese: 白い鳥の羽で製つた団扇を、時々大事さうに使つてゐる容子では
notes.problem: Preciously plies is precious in the wrong sense and has to be re-read.
notes.span: he preciously plies a fan made of white birds' feathers,
notes.suggestion: he handles a fan made of white birds' feathers with great care,
notes.sureness: Very sure as English; no Japanese doubt.

notes.japanese: 竹婦人に靠れながら、棋局を闘はせてゐる
notes.problem: Bamboo wife reads as a person and stops an English reader with no gloss.
notes.span: leaning against a bamboo wife and fighting out a game on the board,
notes.suggestion: leaning against a bamboo-wife bolster and playing out a game on the board,
notes.sureness: Very sure the reader will stall; whether to gloss in text or note is for the desk.

notes.japanese: 縮れた髪の伸びたのを、うるささうに垂らしてゐる
notes.problem: Hanging tiresomely attaches the weariness to the hair, not English.
notes.span: his grown-out curling hair hanging tiresomely over his shoulders.
notes.suggestion: his grown-out curling hair straggling unkempt over his shoulders.
notes.sureness: Very sure as English; faithful check need only confirmうるささうに means unkempt-looking.

notes.japanese: 当座の行きがかりで、糟邱の良友たる孫先生が、この不思議な療治に立合ふ事になつたのは云ふまでもない。
notes.problem: The whole sentence has to be read twice; in the course of things buries the joke.
notes.span: That Sun Sensei, the good friend of the wine-mound, should in the course of things have come to stand witness to this strange cure goes without saying.
notes.suggestion: That Sun Sensei, the good friend of the wine-mound, should as things fell out have ended up witnessing this strange cure goes without saying.
notes.sureness: Sure the shape is the problem; exact wording is the desk's.

notes.japanese: 皮膚の全面に、あらゆる方向へ動かうとする力が働いてゐるが、皮膚自身は、それに対して、毫も弾力を持つてゐない。
notes.problem: Reads as a physics report, not skin in pain, so the torture goes flat instead of squirming.
notes.span: Over the whole surface of the skin a force is at work tending to move in every direction, while the skin itself has not the least elasticity against it.
notes.suggestion: Across every inch of skin something tugs in every direction at once, and the skin has no give in it at all.
notes.sureness: Sure as English that the current shape fails; faithful reader must say if tugs keeps the Japanese force.

notes.japanese: 急に落ちつけてゐた尻を持ち上げて
notes.problem: Haunches he had settled is anatomy-dictionary English and turns grave into comic.
notes.span: suddenly raised the haunches he had settled
notes.suggestion: suddenly heaved himself up from where he had settled
notes.sureness: Very sure as English; no Japanese doubt.

notes.japanese: 霜に侵された双髩が、纔に、顳顬の上に、残つてゐるばかり
notes.problem: Temples twice in one breath forces a re-read and sounds like unedited machine carry-over.
notes.span: frost-touched hair at the temples lingers only faintly above the temples,
notes.suggestion: frost-touched hair at the temples survives only faintly,
notes.sureness: Very sure as English; faithful check need only confirm双髩 versus顳顬 can share one temples.

notes.japanese: 酒虫を吐いたと云ふ事と、劉のその後の零落とを、因果の関係に並べて見る以上、これは、誰にでも起りやすい疑問である。
notes.problem: Nominalized cause-and-effect syntax has to be read twice and kills the dry seminar snap.
notes.span: if the spitting out of the wine worm and Liu's later destitution are set side by side in a relation of cause and effect, this is a question apt to occur to anyone.
notes.suggestion: once you set the spitting-out of the wine worm side by side with Liu's later ruin as cause and effect, it is a question anyone would ask.
notes.sureness: Sure the shape is the problem; wording is the desk's.

data.say: Heat, tableau and expulsion read strongly, but dictionary nouns and two overbuilt sentences stop the English reader cold.
